name: Intuit Inc.

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Intuit sells TurboTax (tax filing), QuickBooks (small-business accounting, payroll, payments, loans), Credit Karma (finds credit cards, loans, insurance for consumers) and Mailchimp (email marketing, being sold); about 93M customers, FY26 revenue $21.4B.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: FY26 revenue $21,448M: Global Business Solutions $11,592M recast (QB Online $5,051M, Online Services $3,595M, Desktop $2,946M); Consumer $8,584M (TurboTax $5,296M, Credit Karma $2,641M, ProTax $647M); Mailchimp $1,272M.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Tens of millions of consumers, small businesses and accountants; no customer concentration disclosed. Credit Karma is paid by lenders, card issuers and insurers (partner revenue, concentration not disclosed).

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: International revenue is about 8% of the total in each of FY24-FY26; sells mainly in the US (and Canada); almost all in dollars, so little currency exposure.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Subscriptions and per-return fees plus take rate on payments, bill pay, payroll and loans, plus referral fees at Credit Karma. Service revenue was $3,933M of $4,354M in Q1 FY27 (90%). Business money payment volume +33% in Q1. Per-customer, not per-seat, pricing.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Capex about $221M (about 1% of revenue); GAAP operating margin 27% (FY26 $5,884M on $21,448M). Fixed-cost heavy (R&D, sales), so margin expands with revenue; 17% headcount cut in May 2026. Guidance hit rate: FY26 revenue $21.45B beat the initial $21.0-21.2B guide, TurboTax +7% vs +8% guided; but FY27 Credit Karma guide cut within 3 months (+11-13% to +3-7%). Cash collected up front on subscriptions (deferred revenue $1.1B).

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Critical inputs: public cloud (AWS and Google Cloud host most online systems), bank and payment-processor partners (some sole or limited source per 10-K), lender and card-issuer partners at Credit Karma, funding for QuickBooks Capital loans (secured revolvers $970M, loan sales). Cloud is replaceable but costly to move. Can pass cost on: QB Online growth cites 'higher effective prices'; Q1 payment cost of revenue rose with volume. Signal tags: rates and hy_spreads (loan funding, Credit Karma lender appetite and demand), consumer_spending_nominal (payment volume), wages (headcount cut). Rates hit Credit Karma in Q1.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Switching costs (books, payroll, accountant network), tax and financial data, brand, scale; now doing differently: AI agents inside QuickBooks, listings in Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, in-house refund transfer, TurboTax 'Sign and File' at a lower price. Edge is strongest in business software, weaker in consumer discovery.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: TurboTax and QuickBooks are household names; about 93M customers; marketing spend rose in FY26 (Consumer marketing +$191M). Loss of either would be noticed by tens of millions of filers and small firms.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Management says it is changing its tax model to 'regain share of total IRS e-filers' and cut tax revenue per customer in FY27; 10-K says fewer TurboTax federal units in FY26; unit counts no longer disclosed. Rivals: H&R Block, free filers, Xero, Bill and Block in payments; share in QuickBooks not disclosed.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Online Ecosystem +20% in Q1 (QB Online +19%, Online Services +21%); mid-market customers +30%. But FY27 guide is TurboTax +2-3%, Credit Karma +3-7%, Consumer +2-4%, total +8-9% (Q2 Consumer guided down mid-single digits).

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: FY26 operating cash flow $8.8B (+42%) but helped by $1.28B deferred tax; capex $221M; SBC $2.06B (9.6% of revenue). Bought back $5.4B (13.4M shares, about $410 each) in FY26, far above today's $272. Cash and investments $5.3B vs debt $6.9B. Insiders own 2.34%; 2023 PSUs paid 0% on the TSR leg; no pledging or hedging.

reads.name: Durability (Zoom test)
reads.evidence: Business software is not losing relevance: GBS +15%, QB Online +19-23%, 56% of segment operating income. Consumer is the weak side: Credit Karma 'below expectations' with a faster consumer shift to AI-first discovery, TurboTax cut price to win share, Q2 Consumer guided down mid-single digits. Not a Zoom case (revenue and profit still growing), but the AI front-door risk is visible in the consumer half and not yet disproven.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: No 8-K 4.01/4.02, no NT filings, clean auditor report (EY) with no material weakness found; FTC order vacated (Fifth Circuit, Mar 2026) and suit dismissed Sep 15 2026; one SEC comment letter (Mar 2024, KPI disclosure) closed. Watch: about $3B gap between GAAP and non-GAAP operating income in FY26 (SBC was excluded before Aug 2026; now included).

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat: pricing power and higher interest on customer funds help; Credit Karma already hurt by higher rates. Slowdown: tax and bookkeeping are non-discretionary but lender referral revenue and small-business payroll volume fall. Stagflation: squeezed small businesses and consumer credit. Rate sensitivity is mainly Credit Karma and QB Capital funding.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: IRS Free File / suspended Direct File remain named risks; FTC order vacated and case closed; Ontario class action still pending; Mailchimp sale to Bending Spoons needs regulatory approval (close early 2027); consumer-lending rules touch Credit Karma and QB Capital.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: At $271.72 market cap about $71.7B, EV about $73.3B. Reverse DCF at 10%/3%: normalized owner FCF about $5.3B (net income + D&A - capex, SBC treated as a cost, tax normalized) needs only about 2% yearly growth for 10 years; on SBC-burdened reported FCF $6.6B, about -1%. Own 5y FCF growth about 22%/yr (flattered). P/E 16.5x trailing GAAP (FY22-FY25 year-ends 58-60x), 13.4x on FY27 GAAP guide; peers trailing: ADBE 14x, CRM 25x, ADP 29x. EV/GAAP EBITDA 10.9x.

status_reason: Price leaves a large cushion (implies about 2% growth), but the consumer half (Credit Karma, TurboTax) was just guided down and tax unit and customer counts are not disclosed; the Q3 FY27 tax season is the proof.
the_mistake: The market prices the whole company as an AI seat-compression victim, but about 56% of segment operating income is Global Business Solutions (+15%, per-customer subscriptions and take-rate money), and the stock fell about 60% from its 52-week high while GAAP operating income grew 20%. Partly right, though: the consumer half now shows real AI-discovery and share pressure.
what_makes_market_notice: Q2 FY27 results (late Feb 2027, date not confirmed); Mailchimp sale close (early calendar 2027) with $3.3B cash buyback; Q3 FY27 tax-season results (May 2027) showing TurboTax share regained.

feedback.note: Credit Karma revenue below plan from higher interest rates and a faster shift of consumers to AI-first product discovery; credit-card vertical revenue fell. Confirms tight-credit/higher-rate leg of the regime read and AI front-door effect on referral businesses.
Business Money total payment volume +33% in Q1 FY27 and online payments cost of revenue up on volume: small-business nominal payment volume still strong, consistent with the Overheat hard data.
